newsitem.title: UK: Nurses in Saudi murder trial launch mercy appeal.
newsitem.headline: Nurses in Saudi murder trial launch mercy appeal.

text.p: Two British nurses who could face execution in Saudi Arabia for the murder of an Australian colleague have written to the victim's family proclaiming their innocence and appealing for mercy, British newspapers said on Saturday.

Deborah Parry, 41, and Lucille McLauchlan, 31, said confessions to Saudi investigators were made under duress and that they were "mentally and physically" incapable of inflicting the injuries that led to the death of Yvonne Gilford.
A Saudi court adjourned the hearing for three weeks from May 25 to allow Gilford's family to decide whether it wants to press for execution of the two women if they are found guilty.
Islamic law enforced in Saudi Arabia allows the victim's family to decide for or against execution, which is traditionally by beheading. Gilford's brother Frank has said he favours the death penalty.
Gilford, 55, was found dead in December at the King Fahd military medical complex in the eastern city of Dhahran.

In a letter to Frank Gilford released to British newspapers on Saturday, Parry and McLauchlan said their confessions were "signed under duress, relying wholly on misleading promises of immediate return to Britain.
"We were subjected to sexual threats and interrogation tactics that confused our mental capacities, especially after long hours without sleep and while suffering severe anxiety," the women added.
Parry and McLauchlan deny allegations they were having a lesbian relationship with Gilford, 55, who they described as a friend.
"Yvonne was our friend. Surely you must appreciate that, whatever the newspapers may like to say, we could have had no motive for killing her," they add.
The women said they had complete confidence in the Saudi court system but added: "We appeal to you to listen to our story and are sure you will then be convinced of our innocence."
Relatives of the two nurses arrived in Saudi Arabia on Friday evening and hoped to visit the women in jail on Saturday, a British Embassy spokesman in Riyadh told Reuters.
"They arrived in Dhahran last night and are here to visit their relatives," he said on Saturday. Family members last saw the two women in March.
A lawyer from the law firm of Salah al-Hejailan representing the nurses would also see the women on Saturday, a spokesman at the firm said.
